\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
We study a complex order parameter $z = x + i y$ with $x,y$ real. A widely
used (but here deliberately WRONG for a genuinely complex quantity)
shortcut some authors use is the claim
\begin{equation}
  z = \mathrm{Re}\, z
  \label{eq:wrongreal}
\end{equation}
which only holds if $z$ happens to be real.
\end{document}
